items.title: Lawrence Cotton Interview, 1996-12-10
items.q: I know David Bordenhouse, he plays like that, another guy, a couple of them around the city that plays like that.

ctx.x: Interesting that he didn't play blues or boogie-woogie. No he played blues but I mean. Not a boogie-woogie.

No he didn't play boogie-woogie. I mean you know, it was almost like a stride, a stride piano that you played. And I've heard that all my life and I never, and when I started playing the guy said, no man, don't play like that, don't play like that. So that's when the blues player came in and covered the left hand with most piano players. Mm-hmm, okay. You know because you know what I see, now you very seldom catch guys playing the stride. I mean there's a few, I know David Bordenhouse, he plays like that, another…
An alternating bass. Yeah they don't like that you know. Why is that?
